items.title: The Outlast Trials Season 7.2 Update Brings Geister Event via Patch 1.67 | 1.000.065
items.summary: The Outlast Trials Season 7.2 is live and appears as patch download 1.67 | 1.000.065. This adds the new Geister event and more.
items.content:
Red Barrels is back with the latest seasonal update for The Outlast Trials , and this one adds a new limited-time event. Players can download Season 7.2 of the hit multiplayer horror game, as this also brings MK Challenges and more.

Console gamers will see this as The Outlast Trials update 1.67 | 1.000.065 , and the complete patch notes are available below.

Program “Geister” is an experiment in convergent hallucinatory therapy designed to amplify unforeseen side effects of the Trials.

Surviving subjects will learn to contribute to a morally hygienic Trial Environment through biohazard collection. Complete the secondary objective for extra rewards.

Find as much escape intel as possible, and make sure to leave the Trial with it.

We need everyone onboard to make the escape possible this time.

Help Amelia! Reagents must find Escape Intel Schematics and leave the Trials with them in their inventory. Every phase of the Community Event unlocks exclusive rewards for participating Reagents. Reaching each milestone phase will get you one step closer to the possibility of Escape.

You are the gentle prayer, the shame ingested and repeated until it feels like your own, and becomes a vector of further infection. Pray for the children, and we will let you out.

This MK-Challenge will be featured in Phase 1 of the Geister Program and is avaialable in GENESIS.

You are the rain, a drop in the flood that will nourish the earth, drown the wicked, and cleanse the filth. Sanitize the factory and we will let you out.

This MK-Challenge will be featured in Phase 2 of the Geister Program and is available in GENESIS.

You can now mark any customization item as a favorite. Use the Favorites filter in both your Cell Customization and Reagent Customization Menus to quickly find and equip your preferred items. Now you can easily assemble your preferred outfits for any occasion.

Expect a follow-up or two to be released soon, as per the norm for major updates to the game.

Save 5% on your next top-up, games, gift cards, and virtual currency at Eneba. Use code MP1ST5 at checkout.

items.title: No publishers wanted Outlast because they'd 'rather invest $50,000 in 10 mobile games' so Red Barrels relied on public investment programs and their own savings instead
items.summary: "Everything was on the line" during Outlast
items.content:
"Everything was on the line" during Outlast's development.

(Image credit: Red Barrel) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 2 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Outlast has long since established itself as a horror gaming staple with an impressive track record of two mainline games, a DLC, and an online multiplayer game that still scares the bejesus out of me. So it's hard to believe that there was a time when developer Red Barrels was unsure whether or not it'd even be able to get it out of the door.

After trying and failing to convince Ubisoft to let him make a horror game and just generally feeling like it was time to move on, Philippe Morin, co-founder of Red Barrels decided to leave and form a small 10-person team with developers from other big-budget studios. Their first pitch: a horror game.

“We thought at first that we’d come up with the pitch within three or four months and shop it around to a few publishers," Morin says in an interview with GameSpot . "And we’d find out pretty quickly if it works or not." Unfortunately, it turned out to be the latter, at least at first.

Morin explains how many of the publishers they approached would “rather invest $50,000 in 10 mobile games than $500,000 in [Outlast].” This was likely equal parts because of how obsessed everyone was with mobile games back then and thanks to how niche the horror genre was perceived as. 13 years later the horror genre is still perceived as one of the smaller areas of interest in gaming, despite all of the amazing games released and the revival of two staples, Silent Hill and Resident Evil.

“We were experienced game developers,” Morin says. “But we didn’t know much about that side–publishing and marketing and sales and all that. So we had to learn on the fly.”

The Outlast Trials' initial playtests went poorly: Designer says 6-year development took 'a f**king long time' and 'a s**t-ton of prototypes' Outlast designer says that one playtester was so upset by the horror series they 'ran out of the studio to go cry outside' and didn't return If New Blood had made Dusk 2, there'd be no Iron Lung, 'and now David Szymanski has got a movie that made $50 million'—so maybe there's wisdom in not churning out sequels

Red Barrel finally had to turn to a publicly funded investment program, the Canada Media Fund (CMF) to finance Outlast, with a whopping $1 million dollar investment. But even that wasn't enough. The developers had to take money out of savings, credit cards, and leverage home mortgages to get the project over the line; a huge financial risk. “Everything was pretty much on the line,” Morin recalls. “Of course, it meant working very long, long hours. We were in a sprint to release the game before running out of money.”

Luckily this story ended well, very well actually. After just five months Red Barrels managed to hit the goal of 400,000 copies sold and while not all of them were at full price after sales it was still enough for the team to get some "pretty significant bonuses."

Outlast would go on to sell 15 million copies as of 2018 and spawn three other games, the final being the recent multiplayer horror game The Outlast Trials which achieved an all-time concurrent player count peak just 11-days ago of 147,955. Pretty solid for a multiplayer survival horror game.

items.title: The Outlast Trials' initial playtests went poorly: Designer says 6-year development took 'a f**king long time' and 'a s**t-ton of prototypes'
items.summary: Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin recently spoke on the trials The Outlast Trials outlasted.
items.content:
Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin recently spoke on the trials The Outlast Trials outlasted.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works .

(Image credit: Red Barrel) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Gamedev may as well be conducted in a black box as far as many players are concerned, so it can be easy to think of a good game as one where development went smoothly and a bad game as one where things went terribly awry. But in the case of The Outlast Trials, making something sickeningly good took a lot of struggle.

As Red Barrels co-founder Philippe Morin told Gamespot in a recent interview , it took six years to turn the vague notion of a co-op Outlast game into something ready to launch via early access. It was "a fucking long time," as he recalled it, and the product of "a shit-ton of prototypes."

"[The Red Barrels team] went too far trying to make [The Outlast Trials] systemic, random, and trying to reach our ultimate goal of infinite replayability," he told Gamespot. "We needed to come back to something that maybe added less replayability, but definitely felt more like Outlast." The article notes that a seemingly shippable build was produced within four years, but playtests went poorly enough to send the team back to the drawing board.

I suppose concerns about replayability have been put to rest now that it's mutated into a sizable live service game with around 20,000 people playing as I write this, though the game's ongoing development isn't entirely free from strife—as the article points out, players are mixed on its use of AI-generated imagery , and Outlast 3 was seemingly put on the backburner after Trials proved a huge success.

items.title: Three Years Later, The Outlast Trials Just Smashed Its Concurrent-Player Record
Steam's best co-op survival-horror is $4 and left me questioning my own sanity
items.summary: Grab your friends and see if you can survive the trials 🧪
items.content:
You can pay $4 for one Outlast game, or $10 for the entire trilogy on PC storefront Steam.

Steam is currently offering you and your friends the chance to participate in hours of gruesome, but hilarious, experiments for only $4. That’s the price of a coffee nowadays.

Over the past year or so, there’s been an enormous and notable boom in multiplayer games. The first-person shooters never went away, of course, but it feels like 2026 has marked the return of good old fashioned co-op fun.

In one of its latest sales, Steam has listed a game called The Outlast Trials for a mere $4, and in my humble opinion, that’s criminally low.

The Outlast Trials is a prequel to the first two Outlast games, which were both single-player horror games. This game quadruples the fun by allowing three of your friends (or random players online) to join you in maze-like maps filled with horrors.

Each level acts as its own self-contained story with some puzzles to complete and baddies to dodge.

Having sunk several hours into this game, I can confidently say it’s bonkers in the best way possible, and on the higher difficulties, it actually torments you psychologically.

Speaking of psychological torment, those that own, and enjoy, games like The Outlast Trials, will get a kick out of SAW Genesis when it launches. It’s got a sweet mechanic that makes it stand out from the competition.

READ NEXT: SAW Genesis has a one-of-a-kind feature unlike any survival horror I've played before

In The Outlast Trials, you’re almost always in the sights of stalking enemies. Some are generic whereas others are more fleshed out characters with unique traits and personalities. The Skinner Man is the most unique of them all, as he only appears when your character’s sanity drops to dangerously low levels.

He could randomly materialise in your hiding spot or appear behind a door, but the best bit is when he full-tilt sprints at you before vanishing into thin air. It never ceases to make me jump and yet I love the mechanic dearly. I’ll go out of my way to keep my sanity in a sweet spot where Skinner Man can jumpscare me, but not actually cause harm. That only happens when your sanity drops completely.

Another fun enemy-type are the Imposters. As the name implies, these cheeky things will pretend to be one of your allies when you get near, but get too close and they’ll stab you in the back (or chest). They’re quite convincing when you first start playing, but the tells become a bit more obvious after a few hours.

That’s the beauty of The Outlast Trials though, it doesn’t pull its punches. Every match keeps me on my toes and whenever things get a little too quiet, I'm instantly anxious about what could be around the corner. It's a tough game even on the earlier difficulty levels, and then when you get to Escalation Mode, it’s straight-up sadistic.

Don’t get me wrong, if you regularly play online with friends the $4 on The Outlast Trials will be well-spent for how many hours you’ll sink into it.

items.content:
Greetings Reagents,

Reagents, hold your breath! Murkoff is releasing toxic gas into the Trials with the new Chemical Leak Limited-Time Event, featuring a new exclusive Limited-Time Chemical Leak Catalog. This update also brings 2 new MK-Challenges, a new round of improvements and balancing updates to Invasion and Escalation, along with new quality-of-life options and other changes to the Therapy experience. Let's see how well you endure the fumes and survive the Therapy!

This update includes

  • New Limited-Time Event: CHEMICAL LEAK

    [/*]

  • New Limited-Time Catalog: CHEMICAL LEAK

    [/*]

  • New MK-Challenge: CHANGE THE PROGRAM

    [/*]

  • New MK-Challenge: FUND THE CAMPAIGN

    [/*]

  • Various bug fixes and improvements.

    [/*]

New Limited-Time Event: CHEMICAL LEAK

Poison is an intoxicating embrace that suffocates the body, just as false idols poison the beliefs of the weak, uneducated, and vulnerable. Shut off the valves, breathe freely, and remember that therapy is the only answer.

Variators:

  • CHEMICAL LEAK -A chemical leak is filling the Trial with toxic gas. Find the valves to clear the gas from each area.

    [/*]

  • SHUT OFF THE VALVES - Shut off the valves in the Trial to stop the chemical leaks.

    [/*]

The event runs from Tuesday Sept. 8 (10AM ET) until Tuesday Oct. 6 (10AM ET).

New Limited-Time Catalog: CHEMICAL LEAK

  • A brand new Catalog is available for the duration of the Chemical Leak Limited-Time Event.

    [/*]

  • Players can spend their acquired Event Tokens in the Catalog to unlock exclusive rewards.

    [/*]

  • Once the Chemical Leak Event concludes, the Catalog will be removed and any unused Event Tokens will be forfeited. Be sure to spend your Event Tokens before the end of the event on Tuesday Oct. 6 (10AM ET).

    [/*]

New MK-Challenge: CHANGE THE PROGRAM

You are the crier, who knows that news does not have to be journalism, it only has to be new. Spread our truth, change the program, and we will let you out. 

New MK-Challenge: FUND THE CAMPAIGN

You are the hammer in the hands of a child, to shatter the fragile swine who would separate success from the government it created. Money is the future of speech. Fund the campaign and we will let you out.

Additions/Fixes/Balancing

Invasion

  • Evasive Manoeuvre: Now counters Backstabs by triggering a STRUGGLE instead, and win STRUGGLES more easily against Imposters.

    [/*]

  • Neuroshock: Now automatically pinged when thrown on the ground.

    [/*]

  • During the Exit Phase: When a Reagent is revived, an Imposter will spawn from a closet to match the new number of living Reagents.

    [/*]

  • Ex-Pops and Prime Assets will no longer target Reagents immediately after a Stab or Backstab.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Steel Trap deployment audio could be heard from a very long distance.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where players could body block other players (You can now push past a player of the opposing role who is blocking your path by walking into them for half a second.)

    [/*]

Escalation

  • Removed Broken Reagent from the variators pool.

    [/*]

  • Improved Escalation run stability to reduce server disconnections.

    [/*]

  • Players can now restore their save after a disconnection or crash.

    [/*]

  • Escalation Trial #21 and above: Damage is permanent throughout the run, and Revives are no longer available, making higher-level Trials even more challenging.

    [/*]

General

  • Improved online stability, including rubberbanding, lag, and disconnections. We will continue monitoring performance and making improvements as needed.

    [/*]

  • Player loadouts are now displayed in the Pause Menu.

    [/*]

  • Rebirth: Loadouts are no longer reset after completing a Rebirth.

    [/*]

  • Reworked Biter speed and aggressiveness, and slightly increased its chance of breaking the chain.

    [/*]

  • Slightly increased Kress Twins chase speed.

    [/*]

  • Slightly reduced Arora throw cooldown.

    [/*]

  • Fixed the price of the Jammer Rig skin in the Project Boneyard Catalog. It now costs 30 (was 75).

    [/*]

  • Fixed the rarity of the Project Boneyard poster. It is now Classified (was Basic).

    [/*]

  • Fixed the numbering of the Hopscotch floor game in the Orphanage, making it playable again.

    [/*]

  • Mods support is no longer available. While we recognize that mods can offer useful customization, some can provide gameplay advantages or alter the game in unintended ways. To maintain a fair and consistent experience for everyone across all game modes, mods are no longer supported.

    [/*]

You are the hammer in the hands of a child, to shatter the fragile swine who would separate success from the government it created. Money is the future of speech. Fund the campaign and we will let you out.

End of Mod Support as of Season 7.1

Starting September 8 with the Season 7.1 update mod support is no longer available. While we recognize that mods can offer useful customization, some can provide gameplay advantages or alter the game in unintended ways. To maintain a fair and consistent experience for everyone across all game modes, mods are no longer supported.

We’ve added several new options to the Settings menu, including quality of life features that were previously available through mods. These are now built directly into the game and available to everyone:

  • Field of View – Slider

    [/*]

  • Camera Shake – Slider

    [/*]

  • Motion Blur – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Film Grain – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Chromatic Aberration – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Lens Flares – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Vignette – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Bloom – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Startup videos – On / Off

    [/*]

  • Toggle HUD Display – On / Off

    [/*]

We will be opening a new general feedback form to continue to monitor our Reagents quality of life and see what other features we can try to add in-game!

Outlast Anniversary Merch Out Now!

It was 13 years ago today when we first entered Mount Massive and faced Chris Walker. Now you can wear a piece of our unforgettable Outlast villain wherever you go! Check out the new Outlast Anniversary Collection:

https://store.redbarrelsgames.com/collections/outlast-collection

We are excited to see you all in the Sinyala Facility very soon!

items.title: Hotfix Patch Notes | Project Boneyard - July 22nd
items.summary: Greetings Reagents, Our team has deployed a new hotfix patch to address the following issues: Improved disconnection issues in Escalation runs. [/*] Fixed an issue where Imposters would not receive a rank when leaving an Invasion early usin
items.content:
Greetings Reagents,

Our team has deployed a new hotfix patch to address the following issues:

  • Improved disconnection issues in Escalation runs.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where Imposters would not receive a rank when leaving an Invasion early using “Exit Invasion” from the Pause Menu.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where the Struggle minigame would not appear if a Reagent was grabbed by an NPC while entering a Steel Trap.

    [/*]

  • Fixed an issue where a television screen was missing a code location hint in the MK-Challenge “Cancel the Broadcast”.

    [/*]

INVASION CHANGES

  • Stab/Backstab: Increased charge time to 2.5s (was 2.0s).

    [/*]

  • Backstab: Reduced the Backstab angle, requiring Imposters to be more directly behind their target.

    [/*]

  • Backstab: Now incapacitates the Reagent instead of killing them instantly.

    [/*]

  • Slash: Increased cooldown to 2.0s (was 1.5s).

    [/*]

  • Steel Trap: Reduced mash time required to escape.

    [/*]

  • Steel Trap: Reduced trigger radius.

    [/*]

  • Steel Trap: Reduced damage to 12.5 (was 25), allowing Reagents to regenerate health after escaping.

    [/*]

  • Imposter Night Vision: Reworked the visual effect while preserving its reduced effectiveness in darkness.

    [/*]

  • Imposter Night Vision: Increased battery duration.

    [/*]

  • Imposter Respawn: Increased the minimum camera time of Imposters to 45s when against a solo Reagent (was 30s).

    [/*]

  • Solo Invasion: Reduced active Invasion time to 3 minutes (was 5 minutes).

    [/*]

  • Stim: Slightly increased injection time to reduce reactive use during encounters.

    [/*]

  • Syringes now spawn throughout the Trial instead of being limited in quantity.

    [/*]

  • Reagents can now use the Regroup button even while Imposters are present in the room.

    [/*]

Remember that if you encounter any issues in-game, please join our 18+ Official Outlast Discord Server and create a ticket to speak with our support team directly.

Thank you to everyone who has been filling out our Invasion 2.0 Feedback Survey. Your feedback will help us keep refining this game mode. We're also still gathering feedback for the Season 6: Project Judas update, so let us know what you thought about last Season's Therapy.

Catch you in the Sleep Room Reagents!

Team RB
